text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Defence Ministry to sign deal for British missiles. Industry experts have said Kuwait is finalising a deal with Britain for Sea Skua missiles despite a demand by parliament to further probe the contract.
- Chairman of oil giant Chevron Corp to hold talks with Kuwaiti officials on March 30. Chevron has a technical assistance agreement with the Gulf Arab state.

- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah tackles Iraqi-Russian oil deal in telephone call with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright. Baghdad and Moscow signed a $3.5 billion deal on Friday to develop Iraq's west Qurnah oilfield.

- Iraq's Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi says Baghdad ready to establish good ties with Kuwait and Saudi Arabia. The two Gulf Arab states have had no ties with Iraq since its occupation of Kuwait.
- Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, considers launching mutual fund, official.
- Washington reiterates firm policy towards Iraq.
